name: gdb
description: The GNU debugger: pauses programs, inspects memory and variables, and steps through code line by line.

flags.description: Backtrace: the call stack at a crash.

examples.output:
(gdb) break main
(gdb) run
Breakpoint 1, main () at main.c:5
examples.explanation: Stops at main — you can now inspect state before anything runs.

examples.output:
#0  0x... in strlen () from libc
#1  0x... in process (name=0x0) at utils.c:42
examples.explanation: A crashed program's stack: process() called strlen with a NULL pointer at utils.c:42. This is how segfaults get solved.
Loads a core dump (enable with ulimit -c unlimited) for post-mortem analysis.

about: Compile with gcc -g so gdb can map machine code to source. Core dumps (ulimit -c unlimited, /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern) capture a crashed program's memory for later bt analysis. gdb also debugs running processes (gdb -p PID).
useCases: Find segfaults and their exact line.
mistakes: Debugging a binary built without -g — no line numbers, no variable names.
